n:
*Translator's note:* The words “about Israel’s victories” are not in the Hebrew text but have been supplied for clarity.

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “he sent to.”

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “and to the kings who [are] from the north in.”

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “Chinneroth,” a city and plain located in the territory of Naphtali in Galilee (BDB 490 s.v. כִּנֶּרֶת, כִּנֲרוֹת).

*Study note:* *Kinnereth* was a city in Galilee located near the Sea of Galilee ({{Deuteronomy 3:17|Deut 3:17}}). The surrounding region also became known by this name ({{1 Kings 15:20|1 Kgs 15:20}}; cf. {{Matthew 14:34|Matt 14:34}}), and eventually even the lake itself ({{Joshua 12:3|Josh 12:3}}; cf. Luke 5:1). The “rift valley south of” Galilee probably refers to the northern part of the Jordan Valley from the lake to where the Jezreel Valley joins the rift valley. Dor is nearly due west from that point.

*Translator's note:* The verb “came” is supplied in the translation (see v. {{Joshua 11:4|4}}).

*Translator's note:* Or “land.”
*Translator's note:* *Heb* “They and all their camps with them came out, a people as numerous as the sand which is on the edge of the sea in multitude, and [with] horses and chariots very numerous.”
*Translator's note:* *Heb* “burn with fire”; the words “with fire” are redundant in English and have not been included in the translation.
*Translator's note:* *Heb* “Joshua and all the people of war with him came upon them at the Waters of Merom suddenly and fell upon them.”
*Translator's note:* The meaning of the Hebrew name “Misrephoth Maim” is perhaps “lime-kilns by the water” (see *HALOT* 641 s.v. מִשְׂרָפוֹת).
*Translator's note:* *Heb* “burned with fire”; the words “with fire” are redundant in English and have not been included in the translation.

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “and they struck down all life which was in it with the edge of the sword, annihilating.”

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “burned with fire”; the words “with fire” are redundant in English and have not been included in the translation.
*Translator's note:* *Heb* “and he struck them down with the edge of the sword, he annihilated them.”
*Translator's note:* *Heb* “but all the people they struck down with the edge of the sword until they destroyed them.”
*Translator's note:* *Heb* “As the Lord commanded Moses his servant, so Moses commanded Joshua, and Joshua acted accordingly; he did not turn aside a thing from all which the Lord commanded Moses.”

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “Joshua took all this land.”

*Study note:* The Negev is an area south of the Judean hill country and west of the rift valley. As a geographic feature it is an arid depression extending south to the Gulf of Aqabah, but the biblical reference is probably to the northern part of this region.

*Study note:* The foothills (שְׁפֵלָה, “shephelah”) refer to the transition region between the Judean hill country and the Mediterranean coastal plain.

*Study note:* As a geographic feature, the rift valley (עֲרָבָה, ʿaravah) extends from Galilee to the Gulf of Aqaba. The reference here is probably to the Jordan Valley and the wider part of the rift valley below the Dead Sea.
*Translator's note:* *Heb* “and struck them down and killed them.”

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “made war with.”

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “for many days.”

*Translator's note:* The LXX omits this parenthetical note, which may represent a later scribal addition.

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “the whole they took in battle.”

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “for from the Lord it was to harden their heart[s] to meet for the battle with Israel, in order to annihilate them, so that they would receive no mercy, in order annihilate them, as the Lord commanded Moses.”

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “went and cut off the Anakites from the hill country.”

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “and from all the hill country of Israel.”

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “took.”

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “according to all which the Lord said to Moses.” The translation assumes this refers to the promise of the land (see {{Joshua 1:3|1:3}}). Another possibility is that it refers to the Lord’s instructions, in which case the phrase could be translated, “just as the Lord had instructed Moses” (so NLT; cf. also NIV “had directed Moses”).

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “and Joshua gave it for an inheritance to Israel according to their allotted portions by their tribes.”

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “and took possession of their land.”

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “beyond the Jordan, toward the rising of the sun.”

*Study note:* The rift valley is a geographic feature that extends from Mt. Hermon to the Gulf of Aqaba and includes the Sea of Galilee, the Jordan River, and the Dead Sea. The section described here extends from the border of Moab, the Arnon which runs into the middle of the Dead Sea, northward up the entire Jordan valley and beyond Galilee to Mt. Hermon at the border of Lebanon.

*Translator's note:* Or perhaps, “reigned.”

*Text-critical note:* The MT reads here “and the middle of the valley,” but the reading “the city in the middle of valley” can be reconstructed on the basis of {{Joshua 13:9|Josh 13:9}}, {{Joshua 13:16|16}}.

*Translator's note:* The words “his kingdom included” are supplied in the translation for clarification.

*Study note:* The *Sea of Kinnereth* is another name for the Sea of Galilee. See the note on the word “Kinnereth” in {{Joshua 11:2|11:2}}.

*Study note:* The *Salt Sea* is another name for the Dead Sea.

*Study note:* The slopes of Pisgah lie east of the northern tip of the Dead Sea.

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “from the remnant of the Rephaites.”

*Study note:* The *Rephaites* were apparently an extremely tall ethnic group. See {{Deuteronomy 2:10|Deut 2:10-11}}, {{Deuteronomy 2:20|20}}; {{Deuteronomy 3:11|3:11}}.

*Translator's note:* Or perhaps “who reigned.”
*Translator's note:* *Heb* “Joshua gave it to the tribes of Israel as a possession according to their allotted portions.”

*Study note:* The foothills (שְׁפֵלָה, shephelah) are the transition region between the Judean hill country and the Mediterranean coastal plain. These are areas of eocene limestone with a distinct pattern of erosion, soil, and vegetation cover.

*Study note:* The rift valley (עֲרָבָה, ʿaravah) is a geographic feature extending from Galilee to the Dead Sea to the Gulf of Aqaba. Here it probably refers to the Jordan valley and an area extending south of the Dead Sea by the Negev.

*Study note:* The slopes (אֲשֵׁדוֹת, ʾashedot) refer to the ascent from the rift valley up to the hill country and to the flatlands (or wilderness) south of the hill country.

*Study note:* The Negev is the area of central southern Judah, south of the hill country and west of the rift valley. As a geographic feature it is a depression extending south to the Gulf of Aqaba, but the biblical reference is probably to the northern portion of the region.

*Translator's note:* The words “the land of” are supplied in the translation for clarification.
*Translator's note:* *Heb* “was old, coming into the days.” This expression, referring to advancing in years, also occurs in the following clause.

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “the Shihor”; the word “River” is not in the Hebrew text, but has been supplied to clarify the meaning.

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “in front of.”

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “it is reckoned to the Canaanites.”

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “the five lords of the Philistines, the Gazaite, the Ashdodite, the Ashkelonite, the Gathite, and the Ekronite, and the Avvites.”

*Translator's note:* Or “from Teman.” The phrase is especially problematic if taken with what follows, as the traditional verse division suggests. For further discussion see T. C. Butler, *Joshua* (WBC), 146.

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “all the land of the Canaanites.”

*Text-critical note:* The reading “Arah” assumes a slight emendation of the Hebrew vowel pointing. The MT reads, “and a cave,” or “and Mearah” (if one understands the word as a proper noun).

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “which belongs to the Sidonians.”

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “and the land of the Gebalites.”

*Translator's note:* Or “the entrance to Hamath.” Most modern translations take the phrase “Lebo Hamath” to be a proper name, but often provide a note with the alternative, where “Hamath” is the proper name and לְבוֹא (levoʾ) is taken to mean “entrance to.”

*Translator's note:* The meaning of the Hebrew name “Misrephoth Maim” is perhaps “lime-kilns by the water” (see *HALOT* 641 s.v. מִשְׂרָפוֹת).

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “only you, assign it by lots to Israel as an inheritance as I commanded you.”
*Translator's note:* *Heb* “now apportion this land as an inheritance.”

*Translator's note:* The MT reads “with him,” which is problematic, since the reference would be to the other half of the tribe of Manasseh (not the half mentioned in v. {{Joshua 13:7|7}}).

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “received their inheritance, which Moses had assigned to them beyond the Jordan to the east.”
*Translator's note:* The words “their territory started” are supplied in the translation for clarification.
*Translator's note:* The words “their territory also included” are supplied in the translation for clarification.

*Study note:* The *Rephaites* were apparently an extremely tall ethnic group. See {{Deuteronomy 2:10|Deut 2:10-11}}, {{Deuteronomy 2:20|20}}; {{Deuteronomy 3:11|3:11}}.

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “from the remnant of the Rephaites.”

*Translator's note:* Or “dispossessed them.”

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “he”; the referent (Moses) has been specified in the translation for clarity.

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “did not assign an inheritance.”

*Translator's note:* That is, “their source of food and life.”

*Translator's note:* Or “offerings made by fire.”

*Study note:* For the background of this observation, see {{Deuteronomy 18:1|Deut 18:1-2}}.

*Translator's note:* Or “promised” (*Heb* “spoke”).
*Translator's note:* *Heb* “assigned to the sons of Reuben.”

*Translator's note:* The words “it encompassed” are supplied in the translation for clarification.

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “princes of Sihon, inhabitants of the land.”

*Translator's note:* Or “diviner.”

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “Balaam son of Beor, the omen-reader, the Israelites killed with the sword, along with their slain ones.”
*Translator's note:* *Heb* “This is the inheritance of the sons of Reuben by their clans, the cities and their towns.”
*Translator's note:* *Heb* “assigned to the tribe of Gad, to the sons of Gad.”

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “and half of the land of the sons of Ammon.”

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “which [is] in front of.”
*Translator's note:* The words “Their territory ran” are not in the Hebrew text, but have been supplied for clarification.

*Translator's note:* Or “it included in the valley, Beth Haram.”

*Study note:* The *Sea of Kinnereth* is another name for the Sea of Galilee. See the note on the word “Kinnereth” in {{Joshua 11:2|11:2}}.
*Translator's note:* *Heb* “This is the inheritance of the sons of Gad by their clans, the cities and their towns.”
*Translator's note:* *Heb* “assigned to the half-tribe of Manasseh, and it belonged to the half-tribe of Manasseh.”

*Translator's note:* The words “their territory started at” are not in the Hebrew text, but have been supplied for clarification.

*Study note:* The Hebrew name *Havvoth Jair* means “the tent villages of Jair.”

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “These are [the lands] which Moses gave as an inheritance.”

*Study note:* This is the area of rift valley basin to the north of the Dead Sea and east of the Jordan. Some translate as the “plains of Moab” (NASB, NIV, ESV) but this can give the wrong impression of the larger part of Moab above the rift valley. See the note at {{Numbers 22:1|Num 22:1}}.

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “beyond the Jordan, east of Jericho.” The word “River” is not in the Hebrew text, but has been supplied to clarify the meaning.

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “Moses did not assign an inheritance.” The word “land” has been supplied in the translation to clarify what the inheritance consisted of.

*Translator's note:* That is, “their source of food and life.”

*Study note:* For the background of this observation, see {{Deuteronomy 18:1|Deut 18:1-2}}.

*Translator's note:* Or “as he promised”; *Heb* “as he spoke to.”

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “These are [the lands] which the sons of Israel received as an inheritance in the land of Canaan, which Eleazar the priest, Joshua son of Nun, and the heads of the fathers of the tribes assigned as an inheritance to the sons of Israel.”
*Translator's note:* *Heb* “By lot was their inheritance, as the Lord had commanded by Moses, to the nine tribes and the half-tribe.”

*Translator's note:* Or “assigned an inheritance.”

*Translator's note:* Or “no inheritance.”

*Translator's note:* The Hebrew text adds, “in their midst.”
*Translator's note:* *Heb* “and they did not assign a portion to the Levites in the land, except cities [in which] to live and their pastures for their cattle and property.”
*Translator's note:* *Heb* “Just as the Lord had commanded Moses, so the sons of Israel did, and they divided up the land.”

*Study note:* On this incident at *Kadesh Barnea* see {{Numbers 14:30|Num 14:30}}.

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “You know the word which the Lord spoke to Moses, the man of God, because of me and because of you in Kadesh Barnea.”
*Translator's note:* *Heb* “and I brought back to him a word just as [was] in my heart.”

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “brothers.”

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “went up with.”

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “made the heart[s] of the people melt.”

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “I filled up after the Lord my God,” an idiomatic statement meaning that Caleb remained loyal to the Lord.

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “swore an oath.”

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “on which your foot has walked.”

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “will belong to you for an inheritance, and to your sons forever.”
*Translator's note:* *Heb* “like my strength then, like my strength now, for battle and for going out and coming in.”

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “are there and large, fortified cities.”

*Translator's note:* Or “will dispossess.”
*Translator's note:* *Heb* “Joshua blessed him and gave Hebron to Caleb son of Jephunneh as an inheritance.”
*Translator's note:* *Heb* “Therefore Hebron belongs to Caleb son of Jephunneh for an inheritance to this day.”
*Translator's note:* *Heb* “And he was the great man among the Anakites.”
*Translator's note:* *Heb* “The lot was to the tribe of the sons of Judah by their clans to the border of Edom, the wilderness of Zin toward the south, southward.”

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “Their southern border was from the end of the Salt Sea, from the tongue that faces to the south.”

*Study note:* The *Salt Sea* is another name for the Dead Sea (also in v. {{Joshua 15:5|5}}).

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “went out.”

*Translator's note:* Or “the Ascent of Akrabbim” (עַקְרַבִּים [ʿaqrabbim] means “scorpions” in Hebrew).

*Translator's note:* Traditionally “the Brook of Egypt,” although a number of recent translations have “the Wadi of Egypt” (cf. NAB, NIV, NRSV).

*Translator's note:* The translation follows the LXX at this point. The MT reads, “This will be your southern border.”

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “end.”

*Translator's note:* The word “River” is not in the Hebrew text, but has been supplied for clarity.

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “the border on the northern side was from the tongue of the sea, from the end of the Jordan.”

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “the Great Sea,” the typical designation for the Mediterranean Sea.

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “this was the border of the sons of Judah round about, by their clans.”

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “To Caleb son of Jephunneh he gave a portion in the midst of the sons of Judah according to the mouth [i.e., command] of the Lord to Joshua, Kiriath Arba (the father of Anak), it is Hebron.”
*Translator's note:* *Heb* “he went up against the inhabitants of Debir.”

*Translator's note:* “Caleb’s brother” may refer either to Othniel or to Kenaz. If Kenaz was the brother of Caleb, Othniel is Caleb’s nephew.

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “he”; the referent (Caleb) has been specified in the translation for clarity.

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “she”; the referent (Achsah) has been specified in the translation for clarity.

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “him.” The referent of the pronoun could be Othniel, in which case the translation would be “she incited him [Othniel] to ask her father for a field.” This is problematic, however, for Achsah, not Othniel, makes the request in v. {{Joshua 15:19|19}}. The LXX has “he [Othniel] urged her to ask her father for a field.” This appears to be an attempt to reconcile the apparent inconsistency and probably does not reflect the original text. If Caleb is understood as the referent of the pronoun, the problem disappears. For a fuller discussion of the issue, see P. G. Mosca, “Who Seduced Whom? A Note on {{Joshua 15:18|Joshua 15:18}}//{{Judges 1:14|Judges 1:14}}, ” *CBQ* 46 (1984): 18-22. This incident is also recorded in {{Judges 1:14|Judg 1:14}}.

*Translator's note:* Elsewhere this Hebrew word (בְּרָכָה, berakhah) is often translated “blessing,” but here it refers to a gift (as in {{Genesis 33:11|Gen 33:11}}; {{1 Samuel 25:27|1 Sam 25:27}}; {{1 Samuel 30:26|30:26}}; {{2 Kings 5:15|2 Kgs 5:15}}).
*Translator's note:* *Heb* “This is the inheritance of the tribe of the sons of Judah by their clans.”
*Translator's note:* *Heb* “and the cities were at the end of the tribe of the sons of Judah, at the border of Edom, to the south.”

*Translator's note:* The total number of names in the list is thirty-six, not twenty-nine. Perhaps (1) some of the names are alternatives (though the text appears to delineate clearly such alternative names here and elsewhere, see vv. {{Joshua 15:8|8}}, {{Joshua 15:9|9}}, {{Joshua 15:10|10}}, {{Joshua 15:13|13}}, {{Joshua 15:25|25b}}) or (2), more likely, later scribes added to a list originally numbering twenty-nine and failed to harmonize the concluding summary statement with the expanded list.

*Translator's note:* The words “these cities were” have been supplied for English stylistic reasons.

*Translator's note:* The foothills (שְׁפֵלָה, shephelah) are the region between the Judean hill country and the Mediterranean coastal plain.

*Translator's note:* See the note on this place name in {{Joshua 15:4|15:4}}.

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “the Great Sea,” the typical designation for the Mediterranean Sea.
*Translator's note:* The words “These cities were” have been supplied in the translation for English stylistic reasons.
*Text-critical note:* Some Hebrew mss and some mss of the LXX read “Rumah” in place of “Dumah.”
*Translator's note:* The words “These cities were” have been supplied for English stylistic reasons.
*Study note:* The statement *to this very day* reflects the perspective of the author, who must have written prior to David’s conquest of the Jebusites (see {{2 Samuel 5:6|2 Sam 5:6-7}}).

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “The lot went out to the sons of Joseph from the Jordan [at] Jericho to the waters of Jericho to the east, the desert going up from Jericho into the hill country of Bethel.”

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “it”; the referent (the southern border) has been specified in the translation for clarity.

*Translator's note:* In the Hebrew text the place name “Luz” has the directive ending, indicating that the border went *from* Bethel *to* Luz. Elsewhere Luz and Bethel appear to be names for the same site (cf. {{Judges 1:23|Judg 1:23}}), but here they appear to be distinct. Note that the NIV translates “from Bethel (that is, Luz)” here, following the reading of the LXX, εἰς Βαιθηλ Λουζα (eis Baithēl Louza, “from Bethel [Luz]”).
*Translator's note:* *Heb* “The territory of the sons of Ephraim was for their clans.”
*Translator's note:* The word “River” is not in the Hebrew text, but has been supplied in the translation for clarity.
*Translator's note:* *Heb* “This is the inheritance of the tribe of the sons of Ephraim.”
*Translator's note:* *Heb* “and the cities set apart for the sons of Ephraim in the midst of the inheritance of the sons of Manasseh, all the cities and their towns.”
*Translator's note:* *Heb* “they”; the referent (the Ephraimites) has been specified in the translation for clarity.

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “and the lot belonged to the tribe of Manasseh, for he was the firstborn of Joseph.”

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “to Makir, the firstborn of Manasseh, the father of Gilead, for he was a man of war.”

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “Gilead and Bashan belonged to him.”

*Study note:* On the assignment of Manasseh’s territory in Gilead and Bashan, see {{Joshua 13:31|Josh 13:31}}.
*Translator's note:* *Heb* “and it belonged to the sons of Manasseh who remained.”

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “The Lord commanded Moses to assign to us an inheritance in the midst of our brothers.” Since Zelophehad had no sons, “brothers” must refer to their uncles, as the next sentence makes clear.

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “he.” The referent is probably Joshua, although Eleazar is mentioned first in the preceding list.

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “and he assigned to them in accordance with the mouth [i.e., command] of the Lord an inheritance in the midst of the brothers of their father.”
*Translator's note:* *Heb* “and the allotted portions of Manasseh fell out ten.”

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “was.”

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “in front of”; perhaps “east of.”

*Translator's note:* Or “the spring of Tappuah.”
*Translator's note:* *Heb* “these cities belonged to Ephraim in the midst of the cities of Manasseh.”

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “his”; the referent (Manasseh) has been specified in the translation for clarity.

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “they”; the referent (their territory) has been specified in the translation for clarity.

*Translator's note:* Or “the third [is] Napheth”; or “Napheth-dor.” The meaning of the Hebrew phrase is uncertain.

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “Beth Shean and its surrounding towns, Ibleam and its surrounding towns, the residents of Dor and its surrounding towns, the residents of Endor and its surrounding towns, the residents of Taanach and its surrounding towns, the residents of Megiddo and its surrounding towns, three of Nepheth.”

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “sons”; “men” has been used in the translation because the context involves the conquest of cities; therefore, warriors (hence males) would be in view here.

*Translator's note:* Or “were determined.”
*Study note:* On the Israelites’ failure to conquer the Canaanites completely, see {{Judges 1:27|Judg 1:27-28}}.

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “Why have you given me as an inheritance one lot and one portion, though I am a great people until [the time] which, until now the Lord has blessed me?” The construction עַד אֲשֶׁר־עַד־כֹּה (ʿad ʾasher ʿad koh, “until [the time] which, until now”) is extremely awkward. An emendation of the first עַד (ʿad) to עַל (ʿal) yields a more likely reading: “for until now” (see *HALOT* 787 s.v. III עַד).
*Translator's note:* *Heb* “If you are a great people.”

*Translator's note:* The Hebrew text has simply “the hill country,” which must here include the hill country of Ephraim and the forest regions mentioned in v. {{Joshua 17:15|15}}.

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “and there are iron chariots among all the Canaanites who live in the land of the valley, to those who are in Beth Shean and its daughters and to those who are in the Valley of Jezreel.” Regarding the translation “chariots with iron-rimmed wheels” see Y. Yadin, *The Art of Warfare in Biblical Lands*, 255 and R. Drews, “The ‘Chariots of Iron’ of Joshua and Judges,” *JSOT* 45 (1989): 15-23.

*Translator's note:* The Hebrew text has simply “the hill country,” which must here include the hill country of Ephraim and the forest regions mentioned in v. {{Joshua 17:15|15}}.

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “and its limits will be yours.”

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “the tent of assembly.”

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “and the land was subdued before them.”
*Translator's note:* *Heb* “there were left among the sons of Israel who had not divided up their inheritance seven tribes.”

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “and the territory of their allotment went out between the sons of Judah and the sons of Joseph.”

*Translator's note:* Or “side.”
*Study note:* This section of the rift valley is to the north and west of the Dead Sea.

*Study note:* The *Salt Sea* is another name for the Dead Sea.

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “to the tongue of the Salt Sea to the north, to the end of the Jordan to the south.” The word “River” is not in the Hebrew text, but is supplied in the translation for clarity (also in the following verse).
*Translator's note:* *Heb* “This was the inheritance of the sons of Benjamin by its borders round about, by their clans.”
*Translator's note:* *Heb* “the sons,” here referring to the tribe.

*Translator's note:* The word “city” is supplied in the translation for clarification.

*Translator's note:* The structure of this list presents problems. In v. {{Joshua 18:28|28}} no conjunction appears before “Haeleph” or “Kiriath” in the Hebrew text. This suggests they should be compounded with the preceding names, yielding “Zelah Haeleph” and “Gibeah Kiriath” respectively. This results in a list of only 12 cities, however, while the summary statement (v. {{Joshua 18:28|28}}) gives the number 14. One should note, however, that the city lists in chap. {{Joshua 15|15}} do not consistently use the conjunction before the name of each city. See also {{Joshua 19:7|Josh 19:7}}, where no conjunction appears before “Rimmon,” but the summary assumes that Ain and Rimmon are distinct.

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “This is the inheritance of the sons of Benjamin.”

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “and the second lot came out for Simeon, for the tribe of the sons of Simeon by their clans.”

*Text-critical note:* The LXX, Syriac, and Vulgate omit “for Simeon.”

*Text-critical note:* The MT has “and Sheba” listed after “Beer Sheba.” The LXX suggests “Shema.” The Hebrew text may be defective here, since the form “Sheba” duplicates the latter part of the preceding name. If Sheba (or Shema) is retained as a separate city, the list numbers fourteen, one more than the number given in the concluding summary (v. {{Joshua 19:6|6}}). Some translations treat it as an alternate shorter name for “Beer Sheba” rendering it as “or Sheba;” cf. HCSB, TNIV, and JPS.
